en.title: Remove Even Nodes from a Linked List
en.description:
Delete all nodes with even values from a singly linked list, keep the remaining nodes in their original order, and return the full list.

The standard input/output format and examples were compiled by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n, and the second line contains n node values. The source has no numeric bounds; on this site 0≤n≤200000, −10^9≤value≤10^9.
en.output: Output the number of remaining nodes on the first line and the node values in list order on the second line; for an empty list the second line may be empty.
en.explanation: The output counts and sequences are: 4 and 1 3 5 7; 0; 2 and −3 5.
hints: Use a sentinel node and a predecessor pointer; on an even node, link the predecessor to its successor; on an odd node, move the predecessor forward.
